monthly_review.summary: You've increased intensity and efficiency this month, trading volume for higher-quality efforts — evidenced by faster pace, higher HR, elevated aerobic TE, and improved running economy.
monthly_review.highlight: Your aerobic efficiency improved +0.64 m/sec per bpm — the largest monthly gain in your log — indicating better oxygen utilization at given heart rates.

goal_tracker.message: You need 4.6 more km across 1 session to match last month's distance — aim for a single 5.0 km run before month-end.

insights.title: Strong efficiency gains despite lower volume
insights.body: Aerobic efficiency rose from 13.28 to 13.92 m/sec per bpm — a +4.8% improvement — while total km decreased, suggesting enhanced cardiovascular coupling and neuromuscular coordination.

insights.title: Shift toward higher-intensity work
insights.body: Zone 4 time jumped from 12% to 21%, and Zone 5 from 1% to 6%, while Zone 2 dropped from 47% to 31%; this reflects intentional intensity but risks under-recovery if Z1/Z2 volume stays low.

insights.title: Stride length variability linked to pace/effort
insights.body: Stride length ranged from 72.9 cm (slow, easy effort on 4/17) to 91.8 cm (fast 3.1 km on 4/22), correlating with pace (9:08 → 7:13 min/km) and HR (144 → 143 bpm); efficient lengthening occurred without cadence loss (149–150 spm).

insights.title: Higher aerobic TE with fewer runs
insights.body: Avg aerobic TE rose to 3.4 despite one fewer run and 4.6 km less volume — confirming that recent sessions (e.g., 4/12’s 4.6 TE at 7:42 min/km, 163 bpm) delivered disproportionate physiological stimulus.

recommendations.action: Do a 45-minute Zone 2 run (HR ≤138 bpm) at ~8:30–9:00 min/km on your next easy day to restore Z2 volume and support recovery.
recommendations.reason: Z2 dropped to 31% this month (from 47% last month), and your lowest recent HR was 141 bpm — you’re currently under-training foundational aerobic capacity.

recommendations.action: Repeat the 5.0 km effort from 4/12 (7:42 min/km, 163 bpm, 4.6 TE) as a benchmark interval session — but cap HR at 165 bpm and monitor ground contact time (<307 ms) to maintain form.
recommendations.reason: That run delivered your highest TE this month and aligned with your best stride length (90.8 cm) and lowest ground contact (306 ms), indicating optimal intensity-efficiency balance.

recommendations.action: Add 2x 60-sec strides at 5K pace post-warmup in your next two runs to reinforce neuromuscular efficiency — focus on landing midfoot with vertical oscillation ≤8.5 cm (current avg: 8.2 cm).
recommendations.reason: Vertical oscillation is stable (7.8–8.8 cm) and near your personal optimum; targeted strides will help sustain stride length gains without increasing impact.

weekly_focus.description: Rebalance intensity with foundational Zone 2 volume while reinforcing the stride-length and contact-time gains observed in your fastest efforts.
suggested_sessions: 5K-paced intervals (3 x 1.2 km @ 7:40 min/km w/ 90-sec jog)
